title: John 3:32-34: no one receives his testimony
english: “And no one receives his testimony” (John 3:32). Yet many have received his testimony, as John himself goes on to add: “He who has received his testimony has set his seal to this, that God is true” (John 3:33). How, then, can “no one receives his testimony” be true, when some do receive his testimony? The difficulty must be resolved like this.

Jesus, having come from above and speaking what he heard and saw, speaks a most lofty and very great testimony about the Father and about himself. And no one receives this testimony as he himself speaks it, because his hearers, who have only the beginning of receiving, fall far short of the greatness of the testimony. Yet even if no one is able to accept his testimony in that way, it can still be received in the way that those who are just now coming to faith are able to accept it.

So “He who has received his testimony” does not conflict with no one's having received it, since in one way it is not received […] those who, from having received the testimony of Jesus, set their seal with firm assent that God is true, having learned that the one sent from him speaks the words of God (John 3:34). For since he is not from the earth, neither does he speak from it (John 3:31). For God does not give the Spirit in part (John 3:34).

title: John 17:11: how believers are one
english: “That [they may be one]” (John 17:11). The word “one” is used in many senses: by likeness, and in many other ways. By agreement, when it says, “The multitude of those who believed were of one heart and one soul” (Acts 4:32); by likeness, as when it says, “For we were all baptized in one Spirit into one body” (1 Corinthians 12:13), that is, by likeness of nature.

And as we, who have Adam as our beginning and head according to the nature of our birth, are all said to have one body, so too we enrol Christ as our head through the divine rebirth. That rebirth has become for us a type of his death and resurrection, for he rose as the firstborn from the dead (Colossians 1:18). We enrol him as head in prefiguring his resurrection: he whose members we are in part, and body (1 Corinthians 12:27), being reborn through the Spirit to incorruption.
